Observed vs potential

+

+ Everything above is an observed finding — your data actually held the + ambiguous value, so the analyser saw the divergence on this render. But a green run + only proves the template is portable for that sample: {t("{{#if count}}")} + on count: 5 says nothing about count: 0. Hand-crafting + adversarial data for every path does not scale. +

+

+ So the analyser also reasons symbolically. For every condition whose observed + value is not ambiguous, it derives the same-type ambiguous value the path + could hold — a number could be 0, a non-empty string could be "", + a list [], an object {t("{}")} — and reports it as a + potential finding. This is a pure post-process over the render: its output is a + function of the template, not the sample, so it is stable enough to gate in CI. +

+ +
+ 0 observed, 1 potential. {t("{{#if count}}")} tested 5 — + portable on this data — but count is a number, and the analyser flags that it + would diverge if it held 0. + Fix — the same rule-free test as the observed case: + {t("{{#if (ne count 0)}}")}. A host that knows count is never + 0 can supply a PathSchema to suppress the what-if + (analyzeWith). +
+

+ A third, advisory signal rounds out coverage: a bare path that resolves to absent + from a present object ({t("{{user.naem}}")} against {t("{ user: { name } }")}) + is reported as a possible miss — the typo catcher — tagged "for this data" and + suppressible by the same PathSchema. +

+
